items.summary: The article discusses the migration of legacy SQL stored procedures to a lakehouse environment with minimal code changes. The migration reduces effort by 50-75% and allows SQL teams to maintain their logic while integrating with modern data platforms.

key_points: Optimal memory dosing for AI agents varies by model capability, with stronger models benefiting from full guideline sets and weaker models from curated retrieval.
The study evaluated eight models across the capability spectrum, showing that saturated models show no measurable gain from additional memory.
Curated retrieval proved both accurate and cost-effective, with gpt-oss-120b achieving significant task completion improvements at minimal token cost.
Memory is distilled from an agent's past trajectories and injected at inference time without weight updates, enabling efficient and portable learning.
Prompt caching and efficient retrieval strategies are recommended to manage costs in production while maintaining performance gains.
items.summary: A study evaluates how different AI models benefit from agentic memory, finding that the optimal amount of memory varies by model tier. Stronger models with headroom perform best with full guideline sets, while weaker models benefit from curated, task-specific retrieval. Saturated models show no measurable gain. The research, conducted on eight models ranging from 30B to 745B parameters, highlights that memory is distilled from an agent's past trajectories and injected at inference time without weight updates. The study uses AppWorld, a benchmark with 585 multi-step tasks, to measure performance improvements in task and scenario goal completion. Curated retrieval proved both accurate and cost-effective, with gpt-oss-120b achieving +16.1pp task completion at only +5% token cost. The findings suggest that memory should be calibrated to the model's capabilities, with prompt caching and efficient retrieval strategies helping to manage costs in production.
items.title: Optimal Memory Dosing for AI Agents Varies by Model Capability

key_points: Google Research finds LLMs often fail to recall encoded facts rather than lacking them.

items.summary: A study by Google Research scientists Nitay Calderon and Gal Yona reveals that large language models (LLMs) often fail to recall encoded facts rather than lacking them. The research introduces a framework called knowledge profiling, which distinguishes between encoding and recall failures. Using a benchmark called WikiProfile, the study evaluates 13 LLMs, finding that while most facts are encoded, recall remains a significant challenge. For models like Gemini-3-Pro and GPT-5, 26–34% of facts cannot be directly recalled, and even with thinking, 11–12% remain inaccessible. The study suggests that recall issues, not encoding gaps, are the primary cause of factual errors in frontier LLMs. It also highlights that rare facts are encoded but difficult to access, and thinking-optimized models show improved recall for these cases, indicating that better utilization of existing knowledge may be key to improving factuality.
items.title: LLMs Struggle with Recall, Not Missing Knowledge, Study Finds

items.summary: AWS launches the Trainium Frontier competition, inviting researchers to design and train language models on its purpose-built AI chips. The competition challenges participants to optimize model architectures, training loops, and custom kernels to achieve the best performance within a fixed time and compute budget. The goal is to explore how different hardware constraints influence the efficient frontier of model design. Participants start with a 50M parameter baseline and can modify all aspects of the model, including the optimizer and training process. The competition has two phases: an initial 30-minute training period and a four-hour phase with distributed parallelism. The final score combines training efficiency and inference performance. The competition aims to advance hardware-native model design and offers prizes, including recognition at a NeurIPS event and publication opportunities.
items.title: AWS Trainium Frontier competition explores optimal AI model designs on purpose-built chips

key_points: GeoPT uses synthetic dynamics to teach AI models physics through particle interactions.

items.summary: Researchers at MIT's CSAIL and Tsinghua University have developed GeoPT, a new pre-training approach that allows AI models to simulate physical scenarios more efficiently. Unlike traditional methods that rely on numerical solvers, GeoPT uses synthetic dynamics to learn physics from 1.3 million particle interactions, enabling faster training and reduced data requirements. The system can predict how vehicles, robots, and everyday objects respond to forces like wind, water, and collisions, with results up to six times more accurate than existing models. GeoPT's ability to generalize across complex 3D shapes and physical phenomena could revolutionize engineering testing, reducing the need for physical experiments. The researchers believe their work represents a step toward creating physics foundation models, which could be used for tasks like simulating weather patterns or testing new materials.
items.title: GeoPT enables faster, more accurate physics simulations for engineering applications

items.summary: Investors sold stocks and bonds as government efforts to control borrowing costs faced limited success. Rising yields are pushing up mortgage rates and other borrowing costs, affecting consumers and businesses.

items.summary: Researchers suggest the United States may be reaching a turning point in obesity rates, with the first decline in obesity prevalence in over 10 years observed in 2023. Benjamin Rader, an epidemiologist, noted that data from over 16 million adults indicated a decline, which he attributed partly to the increased use of GLP-1 agonist drugs like Ozempic and Wegovy. These medications, originally developed for diabetes, have led to significant weight loss for many users. However, Rader cautioned that there is no definitive proof of a causal relationship between the drugs and the overall decline. Peminda Cabandugama, an endocrinologist, acknowledged the role of these medications and post-pandemic lifestyle changes in the trend. Despite the decline, some researchers, including those at the Institute of Health Metrics and Evaluation, predict obesity rates could rise again by 2035. Both experts agree that while the data is promising, more research is needed to determine if the trend is sustainable and whether the decline will have lasting public health impacts.
items.title: US Obesity Rates Show First Decline in Over a Decade, Researchers Note
